draftNote: 3 of five queued off a bottom-two lane: Mr_Meat31 (support→offlane), Cuban Noobster (jungle→carry), Willy Guggenheim (offlane→jungle).

coaching.headline: Four of five lanes read unfavored on paper, but nine fights won to their one turned it into an eight-tower rout.
coaching.team: Draft read four of five lanes unfavored on paper, with only Cuban Noobster's Scarlett clearing Boris the whole game. The early skirmishes matched that read on offlane and mid: Willy Guggenheim's Skylar took first blood on Grux at 2.4, then killed him again at 4.6, before the matchup flipped, caught alone by Grux three more times before minute 11. Xeebs's Argus lost the mid lane to The Fey all game and was caught alone twice, at 9.6 and 16.3. River control went their way too, 16 to 8, with both seedlings theirs as well. We still won the ward war, placing 36 to their 23 and destroying six of theirs to three of ours. The fight at 8.3 was the low point, lost 1-3 at our own Fangtooth. Willy Guggenheim was alive but pinned in a losing lane across the map — the wrong fight to start. The Fangtooth itself still went our way in the same window, a trade, not a clean loss. From the 20.1 teamfight on, a 4-0 shutout at our own Fangtooth, the team won every remaining fight, cashing Primal Fangtooth and Orb Prime along the way and closing out their core at minute 29. Next game's focus: Argus's deaths were the one leak that survived the win — three separate deaths on him fed enemy takes across the game, including one stretch that cost a Mini Prime spawn and two Outer Towers in the same window. The fix is staying alive through the losing lane rather than trading kills in it.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The 20.1-minute teamfight at our Fangtooth was the turning point: a clean 4-0 with nobody lost. Every fight after that one went our way too, cashing Primal Fangtooth and Orb Prime in the same late stretch and pushing the tower count to eight.
coaching.whatWorked: Fight selection was the story: nine fights won to their one, with six of the nine cashed into an objective inside the window. The only fight given up, at 8.3, still traded into our own Fangtooth taken in the same window — the closest this team came to a clean loss all game.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.text: Willy Guggenheim's Skylar: first blood twice on Grux inside five minutes, then caught alone by him three more times before minute 11 — the lane flipped late, five kills from 14.8 on.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.text: Xeebs's Argus: nine kills, the most on the team, but three of his five deaths were credited with costing an objective or tower afterward — the pattern to fix behind an otherwise dominant game.

20.1.call: Grouping onto our own Fangtooth at 20.1 went 4-0 without a single body lost. That's the shape to repeat — fight for objectives already on our side of the map.

24.1.call: The fight itself was won 3-1 and cashed into Primal Fangtooth in the same window, but Argus went down inside it, and that death is what handed over the Inner Tower minutes later. A won fight still needs to come out even in bodies — cashing the objective doesn't cancel what a death inside the fight costs afterward.

26.1.call: Holding the Inhibitor and closing the fight 3-1 came right after Primal Fangtooth landed and set up Orb Prime in the same stretch, converting one objective straight into the next.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Mr_Meat31 swapped out the meta core's peel pieces, Enra's Blessing (an automatic shield for any nearby ally who gets immobilized) and Windcaller (a movement burst for himself and whoever he empowers), for Gaia Greaves and Hexbound Bracers instead — armor, health, and mana sustained off the damage he personally takes. Everbloom stayed on the list, adding a shield and tenacity burst to whoever his heals land on. The trade is peel-for-others versus his own staying power: with 16,452 healing and only 1 death across 29 minutes, the personal-survivability path held up, though the team gave up Enra's Blessing's automatic shield for an ally caught by the enemy's two hard crowd-control abilities, Bayle's knockback and Grux's knockup.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Maco's loadout is Exarch, paired with Revelation and Fervour — the Empowerment Support build. Exarch's major turns every heal or shield he lands into a short buff for that ally, extra attack speed and bonus on-hit magical damage, fitting a kit built around flexing Gift! between healing and hurting; Revelation also trims his ability cooldowns on cast, and Fervour turns his basic attacks into passive team healing. It trades away pure protection, like extra healing received, for rewarding his own aggression — the fit for a support who closed the Inner Tower fight at 27.8 with a personal double kill.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Goldilocks324 built around anti-heal and true damage instead of the meta core's healing-and-cooldown package: Tainted Rounds cuts a target's healing and adds scaling on-hit damage, Ruination drains mana into true damage, and Terminus turns excess lifesteal into a shield. The meta core swaps in Solaris (an empowered basic attack that also heals Kira for half the damage dealt) and Ashbringer (cooldown reduction on hit, more on a crit) instead of that anti-heal package. Since the enemy ran no healers at all, Tainted Rounds' healing-reduction effect had nothing to cut into, even though its raw on-hit damage still worked, a build better suited to a healing-heavy lobby than this one. Her own build's core item, Imperator, was estimated online around minute 25 — reached within this 29-minute game — while the fuller three-item meta core (with Solaris and Ashbringer) doesn't spike until minute 36; she still put up the most hero damage in the lobby, 35,468.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Kira's loadout is Vermis, with Serration and Melting Point — the Auto-Attack / Anti-Tank build. Vermis's major hits every third consecutive basic attack on the same hero for bonus damage based on their max health, rewarding sustained fire on one target, while Melting Point adds extra damage against anyone stacking more than 125 physical armor and Serration adds bonus damage tied to the target's missing health once the major procs. It's an all-offense loadout with no defensive minor at all, so it leans entirely on teammates to peel the enemy's Bayle and Grux engage away from her while she keeps her attacks landing.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Cuban Noobster ran Manta Scythe, Malady, Earthshaker and Infernum, a full ability-and-on-hit damage package, with no listed meta core to compare against on this hero-role pairing (too little tracked data). What's concrete is the gap: none of the four items carry a point of physical armor, against an enemy comp running three physical damage sources to two magical. The jungle matchup against Boris was won clean and objective damage led the team at 34,342, so the gap didn't cost the game, but it's the kind of hole a tougher lineup punishes.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: The loadout here is Thraex, with Savage Strikes and Ferocity — the Sustained Duelist build. Thraex's major marks whoever Scarlett last basic-attacked, boosting her damage to them and cutting what they deal back, rewarding a hero who stays on target through a long fight. Savage Strikes adds flat bonus on-hit damage that doubles against heroes, and Ferocity stacks attack speed the longer she's in a fight, both compounding the longer the skirmish runs — a fit for a jungle matchup that read favored from start to finish, trading away the burst tools a shorter pick-style fight would want.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Willy Guggenheim kept the meta core's execute piece, Vanquisher, and its armor-shred piece, Deathstalker, but swapped the crit-stacking half, Plasma Blade into Imperator, for Terminus and Tainted Rounds instead — lifesteal turned into a shield, plus healing reduction and scaling on-hit damage. The meta path trades for a bigger burst window; what he built traded for staying power in an extended fight. Caught alone by Grux three times before minute 11, the extra survivability likely mattered once the fights turned into the teamfights from 20.1 on, even though the missing Imperator meant less raw burst on his own kills.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Skylar runs the same Vermis, Serration, and Melting Point loadout as Kira, since both play the sustained-basic-attack style. Vermis pays out on the third consecutive hit against one hero, and Melting Point punishes armor-stacked targets like Grux specifically. Landing that cadence means staying in range and airborne off Air Assault, and the loadout carries no defensive minor at all, so getting knocked out of the air, the kit's own known weakness, costs both his safety and the eternal's payoff at once.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Xeebs ran the complete winning core on Argus, Azure Core, Wraith Leggings, and Entropy at a 57.6% winrate, and added Overseer as a fourth item rather than skipping anything from the list. Overseer's self-heal, a quarter of hero damage dealt returned as health, is a defensible pickup for a mid stuck losing lane to The Fey and getting caught twice, at 9.6 and 16.3. Nothing here is the trade-off story other players have — this is an on-meta build with a survivability top-up bolted on, and the losses still came from positioning, not the item choices.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Argus's loadout is Vesh, with The Tenth Seal and Mind Rot — the Ability Damage Mage build; the major turns every landed ability into a damage-over-time tick worth a share of the hit, scaling up the longer the game runs, which suits a poke-heavy kit built around Dread Nova and Particle Shredder. Mind Rot adds bonus damage tied to the target's current health so it still bites into a tankier body like Grux, and The Tenth Seal strengthens the ultimate once he hits level 10. None of the three pieces offer any defense, a bet that the poke and the DoT outlast the enemy rather than needing to survive their engage, and one that didn't pay off on the deaths that fed the mid and late-game objectives.

threats: Chain-CC risk (2 hard-CC abilities, ~1.0s of lockdown): Bayle Kingslayer (knockback), Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Maco) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
